2000 Australian Open Women's Singles Ceremony

Lindsay Davenport and Martina Hingis celebrate on the court following the women's singles final at the 2000 Australian Open. Davenport, the champion, grips the large silver trophy adorned with butterfly motifs, while Hingis, the runner-up, holds a matching silver plate inscribed "AUSTRALIAN OPEN WOMEN'S SINGLES CHAMPIONSHIP RUNNER UP 2000." Both athletes beam at each other, their joy reflecting the culmination of a hard-fought Grand Slam match in front of a packed stadium.

The photograph, credited to Getty Images, captures a defining moment in early 2000s tennis history. Davenport’s victory marked her third Grand Slam singles title, following wins at the 1998 US Open and 1999 Wimbledon. Hingis, already a multiple Grand Slam champion herself, stands proudly despite the runner-up finish. The image underscores the camaraderie and mutual respect between two of the era’s top competitors.

sourceTitle: Henin Claims US Open Crown and World No. 1
sourceExcerpt:
Henin Claims US Open Crown and World No. 1

In a thrilling conclusion to the 2003 US Open women’s singles final, Justine Henin defeated fellow Belgian Kim Clijsters to secure her second Grand Slam title of the year. Clijsters, wearing red, accepts the finalist’s silver platter inscribed “US OPEN A USTA EVENT WOMEN'S SINGLES CHAMPIONSHIP FINALIST,” while Henin, dressed in white and cap, proudly holds the champion’s trophy. The victory not only added to Henin’s French Open triumph earlier in the season but also elevated her to the top of the WTA rankings for the first time.

This moment capped a season defined by the intense rivalry between Henin and Clijsters, who faced off in multiple finals throughout 2003. Henin’s versatile one-handed backhand and strategic play earned her the US Open title and the No. 1 ranking, a position she would reclaim later in the year. The presentation ceremony, set against the iconic US Open court and American flags, immortalizes a pivotal chapter in women’s tennis and Belgian sporting history.

sourceTitle: Kim Clijsters’ First Grand Slam Triumph
sourceExcerpt:
Kim Clijsters’ First Grand Slam Triumph

Belgian star Kim Clijsters clinched her maiden Grand Slam title on September 10, 2005, at the US Open in Flushing Meadows. After four prior final losses, she overpowered Mary Pierce 6-3, 6-1 in just 65 minutes, showcasing a blazing serve, rock-solid defense, and tactical shot variation. 

Dressed in white FILA attire, Clijsters hoisted the silver US Open trophy amid American and Belgian flags, her expression a mix of joy and relief. This victory paved the way for two more US Open titles in 2009 and 2010, and an Australian Open win in 2011.

At the conclusion of the 2009 US Open women’s singles final, Kim Clijsters and Caroline Wozniacki posed together for the trophy presentation. Wozniacki, the runner-up, displayed the silver finalist platter emblazoned with “US OPEN A USTA EVENT WOMEN’S SINGLES CHAMPIONSHIP FINALIST.”

Wozniacki’s Tokyo Triumph

Caroline Wozniacki clinched the Pan Pacific Open title in Tokyo on October 2, 2010, overcoming Elena Dementieva 1-6, 6-2, 6-3. The 20-year-old Dane stormed back after dropping the first set, showcasing her resilience and athleticism. Holding a vibrant red champion’s plate adorned with traditional Japanese motifs, she beamed in a dark jacket and white visor as she celebrated her 11th career trophy.

With five titles already this season, Wozniacki credited her physical fitness and mental growth for her success. Seeded top for the upcoming China Open in Beijing, she stood on the brink of becoming world number one by reaching the quarter-finals. Dementieva lauded Wozniacki’s consistency and court pressure, noting her lack of weak spots and relentless play throughout the match.

Azarenka’s Brisbane Triumph

Victoria Azarenka, the Belarusian world-class tennis player, stands on the court in Brisbane, Australia, proudly lifting the silver women’s singles winner’s trophy. The circular, reflective plate displays the "brisbane international" logo and the inscription "Women's Singles Winner," commemorating her victory at the tournament.

Azarenka turned professional in 2003 and quickly rose through the ranks, winning her first three WTA singles titles in 2009 and breaking into the Top 10. Known for her powerful right-handed play and two-handed backhand, she also secured mixed doubles Grand Slam titles at the 2007 U.S. Open and 2008 Roland Garros. Training in Scottsdale, Arizona, she entered the Brisbane International as a formidable contender and emerged triumphant, setting the tone for her season.

Serena Williams beams as she holds aloft the silver trophy she won at the 2003 Rome Masters, standing next to runner-up Justine Henin. Williams’s powerful serve and aggressive baseline play contrasted with Henin’s elegant one-handed backhand and tactical finesse.
